exposure: Birth mode (vaginal birth after cesarean delivery, planned repeat cesarean delivery, unplanned repeat cesarean delivery)
cohort: The study included 72,836 individuals in Massachusetts with one prior cesarean delivery, of whom 11.0% were Black, 20.1% Latinx, and 56.8% White.
finding: Patterns of SMM by birth mode varied by race and ethnicity, with elevated rates of SMM among marginalized racial and ethnic groups undergoing planned cesarean births.
mod_finding: Odds of SMM were higher for unplanned and planned repeat cesarean births compared with vaginal birth after cesarean delivery, and planned repeat cesarean birth was associated with an increased likelihood of SMM for Black (0.56 percentage points) and Latinx (0.46 percentage points) individuals compared to VBAC, a difference not observed in White individuals.
